title: Deprecate ambient language CI scripts and unify toolchain base image
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: Multiple language-specific CI helper scripts and per-repo ad-hoc Docker builder images have accumulated over years, causing slow cold builds, high image churn, and brittle lint/toolchain behaviour during upgrades. Several repos roll their own Node/Python/Rust images with inconsistent tool versions, which increases flakiness and blocks cross-team upgrades. Goal: Create a single opinionated, minimal toolchain base image with pinned, audited toolchains (node, python, go, rust, docker buildx), deprecate ambient per-language CI scripts, and migrate CI jobs to a unified runner pattern backed by a shared remote build cache and a cache-priming workflow.
background: We observed frequent flaky lint failures tied to mismatched linters and duplicated tool installs across repos. On average a set of frontend CI jobs spend 35% of runtime on tool installation; backend jobs reinstall python deps repeatedly. Prior attempts to centralize images failed due to size bloat and lack of a coherent migration plan. This ticket scopes a pragmatic rollout: build a slim multi-arch toolchain image, introduce a remote cache proxy and a cache-priming task, update CI job templates, and deprecate the legacy scripts with a migration guide.
acceptance_criteria: Publish a stable toolchain base image (tagged with semver and digest) with documented upgrade process
Reduce median cold CI build time for migrated jobs by >=30% compared to baseline
Remote build cache integrated and reachable from CI with an observed cache hit rate >=70% in canary repos
All lint jobs in the canary org use the unified runner image and pass without flakiness for 5 consecutive workdays
Legacy per-repo toolchain scripts are removed or annotated with deprecation warnings and migration PRs created
work_items: Design base image package list and pin versions
Create Dockerfile with multi-stage build and minimal runtime layer
Prototype remote cache proxy (s3 + edge cache) and document credentials flow
Add cache priming job to nightly pipeline
Migrate 3 canary repos (frontend-app, infra-tools, model-evals) and measure metrics
Author migration guide and update internal CI templates
Run security audit on included toolchains and publish SBOM
metrics_to_track: CI job median and p95 runtime
Cache hit rate (artifacts and layer cache)
CI queue wait time and runner boot time
rollout_plan: Week 1: Finalize image manifest and build pipeline; produce alpha image and internal SBOM
Week 2: Stand up remote cache proxy and enable cache-priming job; migrate infra-tools repo as dry-run
Week 3: Migrate frontend-app and model-evals as canaries; collect metrics and fix regressions
Week 4: Broad rollout to remaining repos, deprecate legacy scripts, and update docs; onboard platform team to support upgrades
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: image size grows causing slower pulls — Mitigation: enforce strict layer limits and strip build deps in final stage
Risk: cache auth complexity for private forks — Mitigation: token-scoped cache access and fallback to cold builds
Risk: unexpected linter/regression changes — Mitigation: maintain pinned linter versions and automated evals against a verified test set
